name: Scalp reduction

lead: Scalp reduction cuts out a strip of bald scalp and stitches hair-bearing skin together to shrink the bald area. It has been described in surgical journals since at least 1980, often alongside hair transplants.
The sources reviewed are technique papers and case reports; no trials were found.

paras: Bald skin is excised and neighbouring scalp is advanced and sutured; stretching techniques and serial procedures have been described.
It is a surgical procedure with the usual risks of excision and closure, such as scarring. The sources reviewed do not give complication rates.

lead: Scalp reduction is a surgical procedure in which a segment of hairless or thinning scalp skin is cut out and the remaining hair-bearing scalp is pulled together and sutured, reducing the area of bald skin. In the dermatologic literature it was described as an adjunct to hair transplantation as early as 1980.[1]

Related published work includes serial reductions analysed biomechanically,[2] scalp extension techniques,[3] a device for managing suture tension during skin closure,[4] and use of the procedure for a skull condition, cutis verticis gyrata.[5] The Wikipedia article on hair transplantation does not describe scalp reduction, and no controlled trials were found.[6]

paras: The procedure removes bald scalp and advances neighbouring hair-bearing skin to close the gap. A 1980 article reviewed the literature and presented an improved technique for using it alongside transplantation.[1] Later papers addressed repeating the procedure in stages[2] and extending the stretch capacity of the scalp.[3]
A 1984 case report described scalp reduction as treatment for a patient with cutis verticis gyrata, a condition of folded scalp skin.[5]
No studies found. The literature consists of technique descriptions and case reports rather than trials with outcome comparisons.[1][2][5]

timeline.event: A review and improved technique for scalp reduction as an adjunct to hair transplantation is published.[1]
Scalp reduction is reported as treatment for cutis verticis gyrata.[5]
Serial scalp reductions are analysed from a biomechanical viewpoint.[2]
